atlas-mt.0105: Maltese and English are the official languages, and Maltese matters in the public sector; the Malta Gaming Authority’s careers page is in English.
atlas-mt.0106: In iGaming operations a second market language is the entry ticket: bet365 asks for fluency in one or more supported languages including English, and Betsson’s customer roles name German, Danish, Nordic or Lithuanian. Evidence is an interview and the language on the CV.
atlas-mt.0107: English is the working language in Malta’s tech and iGaming firms; Betsson’s infosec and AI internships in Malta are posted in English.
atlas-mt.0108: No return-offer or conversion rate was found for any programme above: HSBC Malta, Deloitte and the Malta Gaming Authority give no hiring share for their interns. Treat the national figure as the guide: 92.8% of tertiary graduates aged 20 to 34 who left education up to three years earlier were in work in 2025.
atlas-mt.0109: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens may work from day one: the employer files the Jobsplus engagement form by the first day, which also gives you social-security and tax numbers.
atlas-mt.0110: Within 90 days, register online with Identità and collect a free eResidence card, valid five years; you need a lease registered with the Housing Authority.
atlas-mt.0111: Since March 2024 every non-EU student on a course over 90 days, UK and US citizens included, needs a national D visa before travelling; then apply for the permit within 30 days of arriving.
atlas-mt.0112: No work in the first 90 days; from day 91, up to 20 hours a week on degree courses, with a Jobsplus licence the employer pays for and that is tied to that employer.
atlas-mt.0113: A non-EU student with a permit from another EU country in an EU programme can study here up to 360 days on notification, with no Maltese visa.
atlas-mt.0117: For graduates of the last two years or students abroad, with a training agreement, a tutor and the host’s written commitment to cover your living costs; up to six months, 12 at most, not convertible to work on the spot.
atlas-mt.0119: After a bachelor’s, master’s or PhD in Malta, apply before your student permit expires: nine months, not renewable. It does not itself allow work; a job offer converts it to a single permit without leaving Malta.
atlas-mt.0120: Key and specialist employee schemes, EU Blue Card
atlas-mt.0121: The Key Employee Initiative gives a decision in five working days for senior or highly specialised roles; the Specialist Employee Initiative in 15. Both need a degree or three years of relevant experience.
atlas-mt.0122: The Blue Card needs a contract of at least six months and a three-year degree; family joins at once with the right to work.
atlas-mt.0130: The employer applies after a Jobsplus labour-market test; since March 2026 you must first pass a 20-hour online pre-departure course, and hospitality jobs also need the Skills Pass. You then get a D visa.
atlas-mt.0132: Lose your job and a new employer must file a complete change-of-employer application within 30 days.
atlas-mt.0133: A hosting agreement with a research body accredited by Xjenza Malta; no labour-market test, family reunion at once.
atlas-mt.0134: A PhD on a university scholarship comes as a student and the scholarship is tax-free; one on a research contract pays ordinary tax and social security.
atlas-mt.0135: Malta has working-holiday arrangements only with Australia, New Zealand, Japan and Andorra, plus a scheme for young people of Maltese descent.
atlas-mt.0136: For citizens of the partner countries aged 18 to 30: 12 months, once, at most six months with one employer; no Maltese visa fee.
atlas-mt.0137: Up to 90 days in any 180 with no work; since 1 August 2025 a tourist stay cannot be converted into a work permit on the spot.
atlas-mt.0139: Senior roles in finance, gaming and aviation earning at least €65,000 can pay a flat 15% on employment income.
atlas-mt.0140: Rent only a flat whose lease is registered with the Housing Authority (rentregistration.mt): since 1 September 2024 a bedroom may hold at most 2 people, and permit applications need the authority’s approval letter and an attestation form signed by a notary or lawyer in Malta.
atlas-mt.0141: Since 1 August 2025 you cannot enter as a visitor and apply for a work permit in Malta: your employer files the single permit (€600) while you are abroad, and you then get the D visa (€100). Since 1 March 2026 workers must also pass a 20-hour online pre-departure course (€250).
atlas-mt.0142: Students on courses over 90 days, UK and US citizens included, need the study D visa (€100) before travelling.
atlas-mt.0143: Your address is the registered lease: the Housing Authority approval is what Identità checks for any residence document.
atlas-mt.0144: You may work from day one. Within 90 days, apply online to Identità with form A (employment), your contract, the Jobsplus engagement form and registered lease; after biometrics in Msida you get a free eResidence card valid 5 years.
atlas-mt.0145: Workers book biometrics at Valley Road, Msida, bring their €100,000 health policy, and get an interim permit; the plastic card takes 4 to 8 weeks. Students apply online within 30 days of arriving (form N.01): €50 plus €27.50 for the card.
atlas-mt.0146: Your employer’s Jobsplus engagement form, filed by your first day, generates your social security number, and the tax office assigns your tax identification number.
atlas-mt.0147: Your European Health Insurance Card covers you until you work; employees are covered by public health care through their Class 1 contributions.
atlas-mt.0148: Every non-EU permit needs health insurance of at least €100,000 for hospital and medical care in Malta: travel policies of €30,000 are refused.
atlas-mt.0149: If your job ends, a new employer has only 30 days to file a complete change of employer (€600); do not start the new job before it is approved.
atlas-mt.0150: The interim receipt and the employer’s “still working” letter let you keep working while a renewal is processed, but are valid only in Malta: leaving, even for a Schengen stopover, can mean refused boarding and losing the application.
atlas-mt.0151: Students may not work at all in their first 90 days; from day 91, up to 20 hours a week with a Jobsplus licence the employer requests.
atlas-mt.0152: The interim receipt and “still working” letter are valid only in Malta: leaving while a renewal is pending can strand you abroad.
atlas-mt.0153: Leases must be registered with the Housing Authority, with at most two people per bedroom; Identità refuses applications without the approval letter.
atlas-mt.0154: Ordinary €30,000 travel insurance is refused: cover must reach €100,000.
atlas-mt.0155: The Skills Pass may be extended beyond hospitality.
atlas-mt.0156: EU citizens working in hospitality will need the Skills Pass from 1 January 2027, unless postponed again.
atlas-mt.0157: Visa appointments at VFS centres in India and elsewhere take 6 to 16 weeks, with slots resold illegally.
atlas-mt.0158: A reform of the non-domiciled tax regime is announced for 2027.
